hero.provenance:
Every figure below is generated from the same
  open dataset the matters use — data/firm/firm.json — so the money on
  this page reconciles with the billing statements inside each packet.

fees_collected.label: Fees collected · trailing 12 mo
fees_collected.lesson: The number the firm lives on.

trust_balance.label: Trust balance
trust_balance.lesson: Client money is never firm money.

fee_revenue_vs_plan.label: Fee-revenue vs plan
fee_revenue_vs_plan.lesson: Plan versus reality is the discipline.

book_of_business.title: Book of business — fees by matter
book_of_business.blurb: Revenue concentration: a handful of matters carry the book. Fees shown are billed-to-date (worked value on contingency matters).

fee_mix.title: Fee-arrangement mix
fee_mix.blurb: How you are paid shapes risk and cash timing: hourly bills monthly, contingency pays at the end or never, flat and retainer pay up front.

utilization.title: Utilization — billable hours vs target
utilization.blurb: Time is inventory: hours not worked this month are never sold later.

realization_funnel.title: Realization funnel: worked → billed → collected
realization_funnel.blurb: The crown lesson: every dollar leaks twice — once when you bill it, again when you try to collect it.

ar_aging.title: AR aging
ar_aging.blurb: Old invoices don't pay: past 90 days, collection odds fall off a cliff. Every bucket keeps its icon and label — never color alone.

trust_balances.title: Trust balances & reconciliation
trust_balances.blurb: To-the-penny or it's an ethics violation: client funds reconcile three ways — ledger, bank, and per-client — every month.

budget_vs_actual.title: Budget vs actual
budget_vs_actual.blurb: Watching divergence is the discipline: variance is colored by whether it is favorable, not by its sign — over on revenue is good; over on expense is bad.
